title: Safety Risks page added to study the risks posed. Grayland incident log built from evidence.
body: The Safety Risks page looks into how facilities like the proposed Graylands expansion are run and what risks they can pose to the surrounding community. This is based on available data of incidents, comparable facilities and statistics that have been published. Five concerns are stated up front — absconding frequency, transitions between security levels, release and diagnostic error, compliance-dependent leave, and what the CLMI Act's legislated push toward community access actually requires — each linked directly to the log entries and official statistics that support it.

title: Research paper updated: full incident record and official statistics
body: The community research paper has been updated. Section 8 now carries the complete documented incident record for the site, and a new section sets out three official datasets — absconding by facility, assaults on nursing staff by facility, and the offence profile of people held under custody orders — each drawn from Parliamentary answers or statutory annual reports. The executive summary has been rewritten to state the question the paper actually asks: not whether Western Australia needs forensic mental health capacity, but whether anyone has established that this model is safe at this site.

title: Questions on Notice tracker launched
body: Sandra Brewer MLA has followed through on the commitment in her 2 August update: 14 Questions on Notice covering the Project Definition Plan, the Infrastructure WA business case findings, Taskforce meeting dates, campus security, the Criminal Law (Mental Impairment) Act 2023 and Department of Justice involvement, bed capacity by type through to 2029, and the relocation of the Claremont Therapeutic Riding Centre — lodged 11–13 August 2026, all currently awaiting a Ministerial answer. We've built a new page tracking every one, plus the historical questions already on the record, updated as answers land.
linkText: Open the Questions on Notice tracker

title: Letter sent to the Office of the Chief Psychiatrist
body: We wrote to Dr Nathan Gibson, WA’s Chief Psychiatrist — an independent statutory office under the Mental Health Act 2014, distinct from the Ministers and agencies already listed on this site. The letter asks whether the Office was involved in GRAFT or otherwise advised on the decision to retain Graylands as the preferred site, whether site suitability has been formally reviewed since the Criminal Law (Mental Impairment) Act 2023 came into force, what school- and community-specific risk, notification and emergency-response arrangements exist, and whether the Chief Psychiatrist would support an independent reassessment of the site. A written response was requested within 14 days.
linkText: Read the letter on the Correspondence page

title: Petition covered in The Post
body: The Post ran a report on the petition in print (15 August 2026, p.14, ‘Petition for Graylands’, Jack Maddern), noting it had reached 368 signatures at the time of writing. The piece reiterated that this is not opposition to forensic mental health services, but a call to pause site works, release the full evidence base, and hold genuine community consultation before construction begins. Asked for comment, Planning Minister John Carey said information had been provided to local stakeholders including a nearby school and the City of Nedlands — the same ‘stakeholders were informed’ framing already noted in his 24 July reply — but again did not say whether a formal round of public consultation would occur.

title: WAtoday covers the campaign: ‘No one was told’
body: WAtoday published a report on the site-selection process and the change in leave conditions under the CLMI Act, with Paul speaking on the record. The government's comment in the piece closely echoes the same language already in Minister Carey's 24 July reply to us — the Taskforce history, the 'more than a decade' of planning — rather than addressing the specific points raised. The City of Nedlands confirmed a letter is going to the Department of Health this week seeking further information.

title: Door-drop flyer distribution begins
body: Printed flyers are being hand-delivered to households around Mount Claremont, directing residents to the petition and this site. The flyer is now also on the Take Action and Downloads pages, so it can be forwarded electronically to neighbours and shared in local groups. If you'd like flyers for your own street, get in touch.
linkText: Get the flyer from the Downloads page

title: Update received from Sandra Brewer MLA, Member for Cottesloe
body: Ahead of Parliament's return, the local Member sent residents a written update — confirming the current Stage 1 scope, noting the same taskforce also covers the nearby Selby Older Adult Mental Health Service, and setting out a funding history that shows Stage 1 delivery has been pushed back in every State Budget since it was first funded in 2023–24. She's confirmed she'll lodge questions on notice with the relevant Ministers at the August sitting. Full letter now on the Correspondence page.
linkText: Read the full letter on the Correspondence page

title: Reply received from Hon John Carey MLA's office
body: Minister Carey's office has replied to our 17 June letter. The reply sets out the project's history and the current Stage 1 scope. We've compared it line by line against our original 17 requests, and checked one of its claims against the source document it names — both are now on the new Correspondence page.

title: Reply by Nedlands Council
body: The City of Nedlands has responded to our letter and confirmed that it has had only limited involvement in the Graylands Campus Project to date, has not adopted a formal position on the proposal, and has not been asked to undertake consultation with residents, schools or community groups. The City also indicated that it could take a more proactive role going forward, including seeking further information from the State Government and improving communication with councillors and local stakeholders.

title: Website and petition now live
body: The community website and the Change.org petition have launched. If you're reading this after arriving from the petition, welcome — the concerns behind each ask are set out in full on the Concerns and Sources pages. If you're here first, you can sign the petition from the button at the top of this page.
linkText: Read the concerns behind the petition

title: Met with Sandra Brewer MLA, Member for Cottesloe
body: Community representatives met with the local Member to raise the governance concerns set out in the Research Paper. She has agreed to consider lodging Questions on Notice to the responsible Ministers on the decision trail, the CLMI Act coordination, and the alternative sites question.
linkText: See what came of this on the Correspondence page

title: Formal letters sent to six State Ministers
body: The community wrote formally to the Ministers for Planning/Housing/Health Infrastructure, Health/Mental Health, Heritage, Environment, Education, and Corrective Services, with a copy to the Premier and Attorney General, setting out the concerns documented in this research and requesting a response within 28 days.
linkText: See who replied on the Correspondence page

title: Letter sent to Sandra Brewer MLA
body: A letter went to the local Member for Cottesloe, requesting she raise these concerns formally in Parliament.
linkText: Follow this thread on the Correspondence page

title: Letter sent to Nedlands Council
body: A letter went to the Nedlands Council Mayor, Councillors and Chief Executive Officer, raising our concerns and requesting for their support to raise these issues to the relevant authorities.
